changes: Weekday 'rarojaha' removed: 'roja(ha)' is the Nepali word for 'day'. Reading 'ra' as ravi (Sunday) is only a guess. Weekday and tithi are now blank and the possibilities are explained in notes
Date as_written now includes 'śubham', as in the colophon
Notes: added the one-year mismatch between Śaka 1806 and VS 1942, with an explanation

date.as_written: śāke 1806 saṃvat 1942 sāle miti bhādrasudirarojaha śubham

notes: The colophon gives two eras. VS 1942 − 57 = 1885 CE, so Bhādra śukla falls in about August–September 1885. Śaka 1806 + 78 = 1884, which is one year earlier: Śaka 1807 is the year that matches VS 1942. A one-year slip like this is common, for example when an expired year is confused with a current one. VS is taken as the main era. 'bhādrasudirarojaha' is probably garbled. 'roja' is Nepali for 'day', so the 'ra' may be a misread numeral (tithi) or an abbreviated weekday. This text is the Siddhivināyaka/Gaṇeśa caturthī pūjā, so the date may well be Bhādra śukla 4 (Gaṇeśacaturthī), but the text does not confirm this. The weekday was left blank.
